A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a formalism to specify and reason about systems in an open world.
the specification of an open system can be determined by specifying its environment.
we have shown how to specify the behaviour of the physical world in a way which is suitable as the basis for the specification of a software controller for a system which interacts with the world.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the specification of the physical world can be developed as a formal program.

, by specifying the behaviour of both the physical and the computer worlds, it is possible to obtain a specification of the control system which is more precise, and more amenable to formal development, than a specification obtained by specifying only the computer world and assuming a given specification for the physical world.
, by taking a wider view of the software development process, it is possible to obtain a more complete and reliable specification of the control system.
